scope: Theorem 5.5 (Finite compatible cutting) of the manuscript “Positive scalar curvature and uniform codimension-two width” (preprints/Positive-scalar-curvature-and-uniform-codimension-two-width-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 336 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 f67c30579306bd4d), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 26. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. statement: Fix a finite number N∗ of labels and the stage constants in (5.2). Suppose a stage-r packet diagram is obtained by the regular splitting construction of Theorem A.1, with compatible smooth base metrics and a finite common list of positive circle warps, and satisfies Theorem 5.2. After the radial stage, require the complete compact-part/product-end geometry of Theorems A.2 and 5.1. Let j0 be the next label, and suppose every nonempty parent packet has base dimension at least two. Then j0 can be processed as follows. On every parent there is a compatible smooth regular defining function with the prescribed signs on the current forced core closures. Keep its zero wall as the new hit space. To each closed sign side attach the full product cylinder over its boundary. These pieces form a compatible smooth stage-(r +1) packet diagram with the continuous projections described above. The wall on a parent E lies in int Gj0 . The remaining profiles may first be modified, their cores enlarged, and their potentials increased in the parents; these data are then carried to the new pieces by restriction and cylinder projection. There are compatible smooth metrics and potentials, and exactly 399 new positive circle factors on each new packet, for which the entire stage-(r + 1) invariant holds. Earlier forced signs are preserved. The new packets have complete compact-part/product-end geometry. This assertion includes a possible one-dimensional output, on which its scalar lower bound holds everywhere. The operation fixes every old warp identically equal to 1. For a remaining label that is passive on the finite downward source diagrams and the face copies used in their comparisons—constant pole profile, full corresponding core, and spatially constant potential cj agreeing on compared faces—the construction can preserve the pole and core and choose its new potential to be exactly (1 + 3ηr/2)cj, where ηr = 1/(200N∗). At stage zero the single parent may instead be an arbitrary complete smooth manifold with no product-end or bounded-geometry assumption. Subject to the same scalar and separation assumptions, if its data are the radial initialization of Theorem 5.4, the same conclusion holds for the first split. Every resulting wall component and every closed-side component is compact before the cylinders are attached, and these components form locally finite families.
